ipc.contract: one JSON-RPC 2.0 contract over Unix sockets; every client - app, console, gamepad, a script - sends the same calls
ipc.socket_mode: 0o660, group `robot` - whoever may watch the robot may watch what it sees (tof/src/main.rs SOCKET_MODE, GROUP)

policies.shape: every alpha policy is obs[1,61] -> actions[1,14]; robotd checks the width at LOAD rather than mid-stride
policies.refusal: the legacy 51-D family is refused at load with 'observation width is 51, expected 61'
policies.runtime_dep: ONNX Runtime is dlopened, not linked: a missing library is a startup failure, reported through robot.health, and the robot holds its pose (robotd.toml [policy])
policies.ours: our own MuJoCo runs drive these same published ONNX files - out/sim/report.json, policy_file BEST_alpha_walking.onnx - which is why TEST-PLAN's walk gate can be derived from a simulation at all

config.behaviour: read once at startup, not watched; changing anything needs `systemctl restart robotd`
config.durability: per-robot configuration, so it survives an update AND a rollback; the installer never overwrites it. A board provisioned long ago can therefore differ from the release default - EN-02 step 1 reads the file rather than trusting the default
